snippet.title: Not a Combat Drone, But It Will Win the War
snippet.description:
Germany's Quantum Systems’ battery-powered Apex Recordhunter just went from 699 km/h in June to 777 km/h (about 483 mph) in October, accelerating from a standstill in about 27 seconds while flying into a headwind! 

Then the battery caught fire before the return run, so there’s no official record, and in this video I explain why that battery fire is important for learning. 

Apex isn’t the interceptor going to Ukraine. It’s a technology demonstrator built to find where electric flight breaks: drag, heat, battery discharge, and stability at nearly 500 mph. Those lessons feed straight into Quantum’s counter-drone programs as Germany finances tens of thousands of Quantum interceptors to be built in Ukraine, aimed at Russian jet-powered drones flying 500 to 600 km/h. The real story is margin: how much of 777 km/h survives once you add sensors, guidance, a kill mechanism, and a price low enough to build by the tens of thousands.

Join the channel as a member! We’re building a global community of people who are passionate about Ukrainian victory, honoring NATO alliances, and dislike dictators as much as I do: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCnRmC8k3qzn0Qxq-nQOWmOA/join

Glory to Ukraine. Glory to the heroes. Crimea is Ukraine.

snippet.title: The President's Car Has an Identical Twin
snippet.description:
Every presidential motorcade carries two identical armored limousines, so nobody outside can be sure which one holds the President. The doors are reportedly about eight inches thick, the windows about five inches of layered glass, and steel rims keep the car rolling even after its tires are shot out.

But armor only works while the car keeps moving. In Dublin in 2011, one of the limousines scraped its belly on the U.S. Embassy's exit ramp and got stuck in front of TV cameras for about five minutes. Reporters said the President switched cars, then officials said the stuck car was only the spare. Even on live TV, nobody watching could tell for sure which car he was really in.

snippet.title: Trump lost the midterm elections, what next for markets, AI and India
snippet.description:
Here’s why the democrats win & trumps loss in election is a short term negative for the US market, the global AI story and positive for India!

(1) Today close to 35% of US market cap is companies investing in AI, if something happens to AI, Markets in US will get impacted. 

House of democrats before the election, had proposed a resolution that US should not bail out any AI company that fails & should be allowed to bankcrupt! So now that the democrats have won, the assumption is that they may increase scrutiny of:
- AI companies and their business practices.
- Data-centre construction and electricity consumption.
- Environmental impact of AI infrastructure 

This could slow some investments or increase costs for AI companies & hence a negative from the market stand point 

From a Political standpoint, 
- Now if Trump wants to make any Constitutional level changes or wants funds to spend more, will need their approval through congress and hence the expectation is that new war funding should stop bringing the oil prices down & hence supporting the rupee as well. 
- Also US is reaching its debt ceiling somewhere in 2027 post which the government can’t raise more money till they increase the limit which will be a tough negotiation between both the parties & may also lead to government shut down in the US which has happened multiple times in the past as well. 

All of this will lead to uncertainties and market does not like uncertainties  so the US markets will be negative and India will benefit as AI will get impacted & Oil will come down and support the rupee. 

#midtermelections #trump #ai
